fundamentals.networking-basics:section:h.alt: An HTTPS exchange between a client and server on TCP port 443. TCP opens the connection, TLS establishes the protected channel, and the client and server exchange HTTP messages.

fundamentals.domain-dns:section:resoluti.alt: A DNS resolver can answer using a cached record. On a cache miss, it obtains the record from authoritative DNS and returns the answer to the client.

fundamentals.cidr-subnets:section:cidr:c.alt: One regional VPC contains two non-overlapping subnets, one per Availability Zone. Of the 64 addresses in each example subnet, AWS reserves five.

fundamentals.routing-connectivity:sectio.alt: Three IPv4 paths compare direct public access to EC2, private EC2 egress through a public NAT gateway and internet gateway, and public Application Load Balancer access to a private EC2 target.
A private EC2 instance reaches a service inside the VPC on the local route. It reaches S3 in the same Region using the S3 prefix list route and gateway endpoint.

fundamentals.cloud-concepts:section:shar.alt: EC2 and S3 responsibility comparison. Customers patch the EC2 guest OS, configure applications, set S3 bucket permissions, and choose encryption options. AWS runs the EC2 host and hypervisor, and the S3 service operating system and storage. Customers protect data and manage access in both services.

fundamentals.cloud-concepts:section:regi.alt: An application runs in two Availability Zones of one Region. During an AZ A failure, the regional entry can route to the replica in healthy AZ B. A Region-wide failure can affect both.

fundamentals.core-services:section:stora.alt: An application reads and writes S3 objects using bucket names and object keys. An EC2 instance accesses an attached EBS volume as a block device in the same Availability Zone.

fundamentals.core-services:section:compo.alt: An upload to a source S3 bucket sends event metadata to Lambda. The function reads the object using its permissions and writes the processed object to a destination bucket.

fundamentals.identity-access:section:pri.alt: A role trust policy determines who can assume a role. AWS STS issues temporary session credentials. The permissions policy determines the actions and resources the role allows.

fundamentals.data-protection:section:enc.alt: TLS protects the browser-to-API connection and the API-to-S3 connection separately. S3 encrypts the stored object. With SSE-KMS, S3 requests a data key from AWS KMS, where the KMS key and its access controls are managed.

fundamentals.data-protection:section:rec.alt: RPO limits how far before an incident the recoverable point can be. RTO limits the permitted time from the incident until service recovery. Compare both objectives with restore test results.

fundamentals.domain-dns:section:ttl:conc.alt: A resolver caches an old address at 09:00 with a 300-second TTL. After the record changes, a fresh lookup can return the new address while the first resolver still returns the old one until the cache expires.

fundamentals.routing-connectivity:sectio.alt: An Application Load Balancer opens HTTPS to a private EC2 target. Security groups control the connections at network interfaces, while network ACLs separately allow the request and return traffic at subnet boundaries.

fundamentals.cicd:section:artifacts-prom.alt: Staging and production use the same verified artifact digest with separate environment settings. Continuous delivery adds production approval, while continuous deployment can release automatically after the checks pass.

fundamentals.testing-quality:section:tes.alt: A unit test checks order tax calculation. An integration test checks the Order API and its database. An end-to-end test covers the browser journey from checkout to order confirmation.

fundamentals.release-rollback:section:de.alt: A rolling deployment replaces instances in batches. A blue-green deployment switches traffic between complete environments. A canary starts with a small share of traffic and checks the results before expanding.

fundamentals.release-rollback:section:da.alt: In a shared order database, add the new column while retaining the old one, keep both application releases compatible, verify the migrated data, and remove the old column only after the old release is no longer needed.

fundamentals.observability:section:signa.alt: Metrics show when order API latency rose. A log shows events associated with a request ID. A trace shows where that request spent time in the API and database.

fundamentals.observability:section:objec.alt: Over a rolling 28-day period, 9,995 of 10,000 eligible order requests succeed within 500 ms. The measured SLI of 99.95 percent meets the SLO of at least 99.9 percent.
